findings: New raw lines 5-14 provide the objective and two variant routes only. The Checkout Sessions variant is `payment-ui=embedded-components` and Setup Intents is `payment-ui=elements`. The actual old capture date is 2026-04-21 (old raw line 2), despite its filename suffix. November's variant URLs were not read.

Checkout Sessions, old raw lines 51-148, describes Accounts v2 customer-configured `Account` (`customer_account`) and Customers v1 `Customer` (`customer`), a server-created setup Session with sample `ui_mode: 'elements'`, a completed-Session webhook, `Session.setup_intent` lookup and `SetupIntent.payment_method` extraction. A customer supplied at Session creation receives automatic attachment, while the merchant attaches the method after completion when an existing customer was not supplied. Old raw lines 141-237 describe a separate confirmed off-session PaymentIntent with the matching customer identity and saved PaymentMethod ID. The Checkout recovery example uses a new `mode: 'payment'` Session for a different method under the same applicable customer identity.

Setup Intents, old raw lines 281-456, 501-518 and 848-1054, describes an enabled supporting method, a server-created SetupIntent and Intent-scoped client secret for Elements, client `stripe.confirmSetup`, conditional redirect and retrieval/status handling. The setup can succeed, process, or require another payment method, and successful confirmation saves the method to the provided customer-configured Account or Customer. Browser return alone supplies neither successful setup nor payment. Old raw lines 1065-1190 describe the later separate off-session PaymentIntent, the documented 402/requires_payment_method branch, customer-assisted authentication using the declined Intent's secret when `authentication_required`, and optional reuse with replacement payment details for other failures.

Old raw lines 20-34, 251-264, 700-719, 802-834 and 1067-1069 distinguish purpose-specific opt-in, written offline agreement, physically present Terminal flows, and whether attached methods may be redisplayed. CustomerSession is the optional SetupIntent/Payment Element integration for saved-method UI, with a dedicated CustomerSession secret and `allow_redisplay` behavior.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-save-and-reuse-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-save-and-reuse-elements-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-save-and-reuse-elements.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-and-reuse`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-and-reuse provides only two paths in new raw lines 9-14: Checkout Sessions for embedded components and Setup Intents for Elements. In the 2026-04-21 guide, old raw lines 8-237 and 239-1190 describe two ways to save credentials without charging. The merchant gets specific consent and uses a customer-configured Account or Customer as appropriate. Checkout setup mode creates a Session and a successful completion lets the merchant read the linked SetupIntent and PaymentMethod. An existing customer specified at creation receives automatic attachment, while otherwise the merchant attaches the method. In direct Setup Intents the merchant creates the Intent, the buyer completes Elements setup with confirmSetup, and the return page retrieves the Intent and distinguishes succeeded, processing and requires_payment_method. A later server-created off-session PaymentIntent attempts the charge separately. After the Checkout branch's HTTP 402 and requires_payment_method, the buyer returns to a new payment-mode Checkout Session with the same customer identity to pay with a replacement method. In the direct SetupIntent branch the buyer can authenticate the declined later PaymentIntent or replace its payment details, depending on the failure. source-stripe-save-and-reuse-elements.md captures both flows but makes attachment unconditional and omits material identity, consent and status qualifications.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-and-reuse, new raw lines 9-14 replace presentation of the full 2026-04-21 variants in old raw lines 8-1312 with navigation. No payment behavior change is established. Keep the April Checkout automatic/manual attachment split and Session webhook, Account/Customer and SetupIntent-specific secret distinctions, permission terms and written agreement, setup outcomes and off-session recovery. In old raw lines 183-237, Checkout recovers an HTTP 402 with a new payment-mode Session for the same customer identity. Old raw lines 1156-1190 allow buyer-assisted authentication or replacement details on the later declined PaymentIntent in the direct SetupIntent route. The Saved Payment Methods concept should explicitly include setup independent of an initial charge, as its existing source link already does. Keep April-only Radar, Apple Pay and Link details as scoped documentation, and remove unsupported Checkout-wide exclusions or automatic prefill from source-stripe-save-and-reuse-elements.md. Keep manual SetupIntent method-list examples as historically dated in light of the separately captured 2026-08-26.preview endpoint change. Retain the older full raw, add the November index as navigation, and preserve the reciprocal provider-index and Stripe Saved Payment Methods concept routes.
